comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Live-run finding + design pivot (2026-08-14).

Ran the first live-Cloud draft against REB+DIG on an isolated S3 store copy. The first scenario FAILED at the read-only preview step (no production impact): the harness seeded dummy project keys (REBEMPTY, REBGHOST) that exist only in the mapping, never in Jira. Real Jira parse-errors on a non-existent key ('the value "rebempty" does not exist for the field "project"'), acli exits 1, and the inbound fetcher (_build_snapshot, no per-project try/except) propagates that and aborts the whole pass. The stateful fake transport all other stories use returned empty for unknown projects, masking this. Reproduced read-only: 'project = REBEMPTY' errors; 'project = REB' with an impossible filter returns []. Engine review found NO contract that a mapped-but-absent project should be tolerated — the inbound search is deliberately fail-closed (correct for a bridge).

Root cause: harness design flaw (not a product bug) — the plan assumed querying a non-existent project returns empty; it errors. Compounded by only two real Cloud projects existing, which cannot faithfully model three repo shapes + empty + unknown paths.

Pivot (user-directed, option A + DC): rework the rehearsal to run against the ephemeral Jira DC instance the existing tests/external/live_jira_dc harness stands up in CI, where we hold admin rights and can create/destroy throwaway projects per run. This makes the rehearsal a reproducible, CI-verified green run in the jira-dc-harness job (not a manual operator-attested Cloud run), dissolves the two-project constraint, models 'empty' with a real empty project, and models 'unknown' as its true fail-closed behaviour. Description + file_impact + ACs rewritten accordingly; the ACs now require a green DC run. Re-running plan-review next.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: PS5 of Gerrit 1790: fixed a real correctness defect the LLM-Review surfaced before spending the live DC run. A LIVE bridge_sync returns NO 'plan' in its details — reconcile.py only populates result['plan'] in no-write/preview mode (nowrite_plan; reconcile.py:742-749). So the harness's post-create waits keyed on sync's plan never fired (flaky index-lag reads) and scenario 1's {one,two} <= _planned_projects(sync) would deterministically fail on empty. Fix: (a) added _wait_label_count() that polls the transport label search to absorb DC Lucene index lag (no plan/key needed); replaced every sync-plan wait loop with it; (b) scenario 1 now asserts the positive subset on the PREVIEW plan plus sync details.mutations_applied>=2. Also split scenario 7's combined pytest.raises so BOTH preview and the mutating sync legs are independently asserted fail-closed, and dropped scenario 1's tautological mapping re-read. Local: ruff/format/mypy clean, 10 collected. Authoritative live validation is the CI jira-dc-harness run (external-integration.yml), dispatched against main after this lands (the Verified gate skips the external tier).

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: PS6: fixed a second real defect LLM-Review surfaced. The library never propagates the applier's CrossProjectTargetError: run_pass_result wraps reconcile_once in 'except Exception' (__main__.py:_reconcile_exception_result -> OPERATIONAL_FAILURE) and _bridge_run re-raises it as rebar.RebarError with message 'ERROR: reconcile_once raised: refusing to apply ... outside the configured scope ...'. So scenarios 6 & 8's pytest.raises(CrossProjectTargetError) would have FAILED the live run. Fix: expect rebar.RebarError with match='outside the configured scope' (asserts fail-closed AND the correct reason). Also pinned scenario 7's two legs from bare Exception to rebar.RebarError. Local ruff/format/mypy clean, 10 collected. All pytest.raises expectations audited: 6/7/8 -> RebarError (library-wrapped), 9 -> StoreIncompatibleError (direct call), 10 -> Exception (direct transport 404).

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: PS7 (LLM-Review+1 PASS on PS6, no correctness findings — convergence reached). PS6's 3 advisories were all non-blocking quality nits; dispositions: (1) FIXED — duplicated docstring clause in scenario 6 ('bridge_sync must raise bridge_sync must raise'), my editing artifact. (2) ACCEPTED — scenario 7 bare pytest.raises(rebar.RebarError) without match=: fail-closed is already proven by the before/after 'after == before' no-mutation assertion on BOTH legs; adding a match= on the wrapped JQL-400 message would over-pin to text I have not observed live and risks failing the run for the wrong reason. (3) ACCEPTED — scenario 1 'applied >= 2' soft floor: exact '== 2' gambles on inbound mutations-per-issue cardinality I have not observed live; the flood fix + freshly-provisioned scratch keys guarantee no OTHER in-scope inbound issues exist, so the floor cannot be inflated by production tickets. Both (2)/(3) will be revisited against the live run's observed messages/counts.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: PS7 LLM-Review+1 PASS (2nd consecutive PASS, zero correctness findings = convergence). 2 non-blocking advisories, both test-sensitivity: (L409) negative 'no contamination' assertions in scenarios 3/8 read _keys_by_label(...)==[] immediately post-sync without an index-settle — a real false-NEGATIVE risk (index lag could hide leaked contamination -> spurious PASS). (L679) scenario 10's _InjectedScenarioFailure is synthetic (raised in-test), so it proves the harness's OWN cleanup wiring, not the product's internal cleanup path. Disposition: ACCEPT both for landing, HARDEN post-live. Neither can FAIL the green run; a false-negative stays green. Calibrating index-lag settle-barriers requires the DC's observed indexing timing, so guessing pre-live risks another wrong iteration (cf. the message-match / mutation-count advisories). Will revisit L409 with a settle barrier and L679's product-path coverage against the live run's observed behavior, filing follow-ups if warranted.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
RCA — 3 RED live DC scenarios (run 31853325667), all TEST-precondition bugs (product correct). Fix pushed as Gerrit 1801.

**Scenario 4** `test_absent_project_resolves_to_legacy_default`: `--only`/`--except` selection (`reconcile_helpers.resolve_selection`) resolves canonical local ids and Jira keys but NOT aliases. The scenario passed the ticket ALIAS to `only=[tid]` → `RebarError: unresolved --only/--except identifier(s)`. Fix: added `return_id` to `_make_outbound_ticket`; scenario scopes the pass to the canonical id.

**Scenario 8** `test_promote_only_binding_is_one_way`: the promote-only guard fires at `rebar.edit_ticket` time (refusing to overwrite an existing binding) — earlier than sync, so the re-point never reaches the applier. The test wrongly expected `bridge_sync` to raise. Fix: wrap `edit_ticket(bridge_project=two)` in `pytest.raises(match="promote-only")`; drop the sync-raises block.

**Scenario 9** `test_capability_stamp_and_fail_closed`: `bridge_projects_set` writes the mapping to the WORKTREE but never commits it. The base copy's `scrub_bridge_state(commit=True)` committed the `projects.json` blob's REMOVAL, so `run_ensures`'s `projects-seed` unit (tree-check keyed on the committed blob) re-seeds a legacy-only mapping over the worktree (project_count → 0) BEFORE `projects-compat-stamp` reads it → stamp no-ops. Reproduced locally on a production-store copy (STAMP PRESENT: False), and confirmed the fix (commit the mapping first → projects-seed skips → STAMP PRESENT: True). In normal production a committed blob always exists, so this vulnerable state never arises — it is a fixture artifact, not a product bug.

Residual: (a) `--only`/`--except` not resolving aliases is a latent UX gap (aliases are the preferred WRITE form per AGENTS.md); (b) `bridge_projects_set` leaving the mapping uncommitted is a latent durability seam. Both pre-existing, out of 368f scope; noting for follow-up.

Next: LLM-Review+1 + Verified+1 on 1801, Submit, re-run the live DC harness GREEN, then close.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

Every other story in this epic is validated against fixtures and a stateful fake transport — the
right tier for each. But a fake cannot reach the failure modes that only appear against a real
tracker: real JQL over several projects, real per-project key allocation and issue creation, and the
one that matters most — whether a pass scoped to one project can contaminate another. It is the
justified live canary the shared test-design standard allows for external-service mapping.

A first live-Cloud draft (against the shared REB + DIG projects) surfaced two flaws the fake had
masked, making live Cloud the wrong tier:

1. Non-existent project keys parse-ERROR, they do not return empty. The draft modelled the
   "configured but empty" and "unknown to the tracker" paths with keys that live only in the mapping,
   never in Jira. Real Jira rejects `project = REBEMPTY` (`the value 'rebempty' does not exist for the
   field 'project'`), acli exits non-zero, and because the inbound fetcher fans a per-project query
   out with no per-project try/except (`fetcher.py` `_build_snapshot`), that aborts the ENTIRE pass.
   The fake returned empty, so nothing caught it. No contract says a mapped-but-absent project is
   tolerated; the inbound search is deliberately fail-closed, the safe posture for a bridge.
2. Only two real Cloud projects exist. Modelling three repo shapes (one/two/zero repos), an empty
   project, and an unknown-project fail-closed path needs more isolated projects than two shared
   production projects supply, and throwaway Cloud projects are not available here.

## Approach

Rehearse against the ephemeral Jira Data Center instance the existing DC harness
(`tests/external/live_jira_dc/`) already stands up in CI, where we hold admin rights and create and
destroy throwaway projects per run. This dissolves both flaws and makes the rehearsal a reproducible,
CI-verified green run on every build (the `jira-dc-harness` job) rather than a manual attested
live-Cloud step. The isolated store copy is the harness's existing local/file-based copy
(`REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=off`); no S3 remote is involved.

A per-run fixture provisions four scratch projects via the harness's bug-3fe5-hardened provisioning
(pinned `_PROJECT_TEMPLATE`; `_assert_project_capabilities` verifies issue types/fields first, no
silent degrade), each a random `RBJ`-prefixed key, and tears them all down on
every exit path: P_ONE -> one repo, P_TWO -> two repos, P_ZERO -> zero repos, P_LEGACY -> the legacy
default. "Configured but empty of issues" is now a REAL project that simply returns `[]` in a pass,
never a non-existent key. "Unknown to Jira" is modelled as its true product behaviour: a key never
created is configured and the harness asserts the pass FAILS CLOSED (the per-project search raises,
the pass writes nothing).

Dry-run gating is the contamination control: each mutating scenario runs `bridge preview` first and
asserts the previewed mutation set contains ONLY targets in the intended project (empty intersection
against every other configured project) before `bridge sync` runs — every mutating pass, including
any binding setup sync, is preview-gated first. The per-mutation target project each intersection is
computed against is read from the preview plan: the Jira key prefix for an outbound UPDATE, and the
`_bridge_target_project` field for an outbound CREATE (which has no key yet).

Cleanup runs on every exit path: session-scoped finalizers DELETE each scratch project
(`/rest/api/2/project/{key}`, poll-until-404), which removes its issues; per-run random keys mean no
run touches another's data, and a session guard refuses to start if a prior `RBJ*` project leaked.

## Scope

- `tests/external/live_jira_dc/conftest.py` (edit) — add a session-scoped `scratch_projects` fixture
  that yields N verified scratch projects, REUSING the existing in-conftest provisioning
  (`_create_scratch_project` / `_assert_project_capabilities` / `_random_project_key` / `_request`),
  and tears them all down. Nothing is relocated: ccf6 and
  `test_live_jira_dc_conftest.py::test_the_monkeypatched_surface_is_still_defined_in_conftest` require
  `_request` and the provisioning helpers to stay DEFINED in conftest (two unit tests monkeypatch
  `_request` in conftest's namespace, and moving them fails open to live HTTP), so the cluster is
  reused in place, never moved. The module-size cap applies only to `src/rebar`, so this test file
  may grow.
- `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_multi_project_rehearsal.py` (new) — the scenarios and per-run
  fixtures (four scratch projects, isolated DC store copy mapped for them, DC-pointed bridge config).
- `docs/jira-sync-setup.md` (edit) — runbook: the rehearsal now runs against the ephemeral DC
  instance in CI (and locally via `make jira-dc-up`), replacing the live-Cloud section.
- `tests/external/live_multi_project/conftest.py` (delete) and
  `tests/external/live_multi_project/test_multi_project_rehearsal.py` (delete) — the flawed
  live-Cloud-only draft, replaced by the DC rehearsal.

## Testing

Tier: a live end-to-end rehearsal against a real Jira DC instance — permitted by the shared standard
for external-service mapping when a fake cannot reach the mechanism (genuine cross-project isolation,
real JQL over several projects). Gated to the opt-in external suite (`REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL=1`, the
DC-readiness sentinel) and run in the `jira-dc-harness` CI job (`pytest -m external
tests/external/live_jira_dc`) on a native-amd64 runner; a new file there is collected automatically.
The nine scenarios are the Acceptance Criteria below, each preview-gated then applied.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The rehearsal provisions its throwaway scratch projects with the hardened pinned template and
      verifies their capabilities before any scenario runs; checked by asserting each created project
      reports the required issue types/fields (a degrade fails provisioning, not a later scenario).
- [x] Issues created in two scratch projects are both ingested in one pass with the correct source
      project and repos recorded; checked by querying both projects and asserting both tickets' fields.
- [x] Rebar-created tickets targeting each project land in that project only; checked by querying the
      projects and asserting each issue exists in exactly one.
- [x] A ticket with an explicit empty project creates no issue in any project; checked by a post-run
      query of every scratch project finding no issue for it.
- [x] All three repo configurations (one/two/zero repos) produce the expected repos on inbound
      tickets and correct routing on outbound ones; checked per configuration.
- [x] An outbound update targeting a project outside the configured scope is surfaced in `bridge
      preview`'s planned mutation set and, on `bridge sync`, raises `CrossProjectTargetError` from the
      write-path guard and changes nothing; checked by comparing the projects' issue state before and
      after the refused sync.
- [x] A project key never created in the DC instance, when configured in the mapping, makes a bridge
      pass fail closed and write nothing; checked by asserting the pass errors and a post-run query of
      the real projects shows no change.
- [x] Every scenario's preview contained only targets in its intended project; checked by asserting an
      empty intersection against every other configured project for each preview.
- [x] The whole rehearsal runs green in the `jira-dc-harness` CI job against the ephemeral DC instance;
      checked by the job passing (not skipped — the fail-on-all-skip canary enforces at least one live
      scenario executed).
- [x] Every scratch project the run created is deleted on teardown and a read of each returns 404,
      including when a scenario fails mid-run; checked by injecting a post-creation failure into one
      scenario and asserting all scratch projects are gone (404) after teardown.
